title: Surface cosmic-ray effective dose scenarios
institution: Jian Zhang and Jingnan Guo, JGR: Planets (2022)
description: MarsPath reconstructs a scenario field using the authors’ published surface pressure grid and six AtRIS effective dose simulations. The numerical sources are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5953666.
format: Figure 2 pressure array, Figure 11 effective-dose table, derived static raster
coverage: Pressure nodes from 89° S to 89° N retained. Masked outside 82 to 1,200 Pa.
resolution: 1° pressure export and six simulated pressures. Display raster 1440 × 720.
units: mSv/year, modelled surface effective dose rate
crs: Mars east-positive planetocentric longitude and latitude
processing: Bilinear pressure sampling with periodic longitude and piecewise linear interpolation of published rates at the surface for 700 MV. Pressure snapshot at Ls 0° and local midnight. No image-to-number conversion.
limitations: Galactic cosmic rays and secondaries, uniform dry regolith and no extra shielding. Solar particle events, personal exposure and route costs are outside this product. Absolute geographic dose accuracy is unknown.
usage: Figure data CC BY 4.0. Jian Zhang and Jingnan Guo (2022), transformed by MarsPath. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Estimated Radiation Dosage on Mars, PIA03480
institution: NASA / Jet Propulsion Laboratory / Johnson Space Center
description: NASA’s 2002 illustration shows historical cosmic-ray dose-equivalent estimates informed by Odyssey MARIE and MOLA. MarsPath displays an approximate geographic reprojection and the original illustration.
format: 3000 × 2400 source TIFF and JPEG, WebP map derivative
coverage: About 79.8% of Mars by area after masking views close to the limbs
resolution: Original numerical model grid unknown. 1440 × 720 display raster.
units: Original colour legend in rem/year of estimated dose equivalent. No point values.
crs: Two independently fitted orthographic views reprojected to the MarsPath planetocentric grid
processing: Fit both discs using the printed graticule and check the fit against other grid intersections and mapped landmarks. Use the more face-on view and leave the unverified edges transparent.
limitations: Reference artwork with uncertain original model settings and approximate alignment. Excluded from numerical inspection, analysis and scoring.
usage: NASA/Jet Propulsion Laboratory/JSC. Reprojected by MarsPath under the JPL Image Use Policy. https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/jpl-image-use-policy/

title: NASA Mars Trek WMTS imagery
description: Global Viking and MOLA visualization; regional CTX and HiRISE mosaics. Coverage and native resolution vary. Imagery is not numerical elevation.
resolution: 232 m Viking; 463 m MOLA relief; 6 m CTX; 0.25 m HiRISE native source imagery
crs: NASA published angular Mars matrices / explicit Mars sphere in app
processing: Direct NASA WMTS; capabilities-derived tile grids and coverage
limitations: No global sub-metre coverage; imagery and terrain resolutions differ
usage: Credit NASA/JPL/USGS and product contributors; see original product metadata

title: MGS MOLA global DEM, 463 m
description: Preserved supplied 46,080 × 23,040 int16 global DEM. V2 numerical elevation overlay and coarse terrain derivative average to 1440 × 720 cells.
resolution: 463.0935 m projected source; V2 derived cells 0.25° (~14.8 km north–south; east–west varies with latitude)
processing: Rasterio average resampling; periodic longitude and latitude-corrected finite-difference slopes. Cell means hide local terrain. See processed metadata and checksums.
limitations: Interpolated gaps, sparse polar data; no rock-scale hazards
usage: CC0/public domain per USGS product metadata

title: Mars 2020 TRN CTX DTM mosaic, 20 m
description: Native numerical elevation grid for supported Jezero routing; 1,596 × 1,512 samples. Research-grade terrain analysis, not astronaut safety validation.
format: Source GeoTIFF float32; browser little-endian arrays
processing: Native grid, no elevation resampling. Invalid sentinel and nonfinite cells masked. Centred finite differences; edge derivatives one-sided. Slope unavailable next to missing terrain. Little-endian float32 arrays.
limitations: 20 m projected grid does not resolve rocks or guarantee traversability.; High-resolution imagery is not high-resolution elevation.; Grid slope and edge grade do not capture every hazard.
usage: USGS product requests author citation; see Fergason et al. 2020 / original metadata

title: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

processing: Normalize 0–360°E to −180–180° for display
limitations: Large regions represented by approximate centres; not local science targets
usage: Cite original IAU/USGS records

title: Mars Climate Database v6.2
description: Numerical MCD 6.2 web export: temperature, pressure and horizontal wind speed. Ls 21.3°, local 00:00 at every longitude, 10 m above local surface, climatology average solar scenario. Model means, not weather.
format: ASCII numerical export → locked JSON fields and interpolated PNGs
coverage: Global nodes including poles and duplicate date-line endpoints
resolution: 64 × 48 export nodes (5.714° longitude × 3.830° latitude); native model resolution not established by this export
processing: Reconstructed producer linspace coordinates because ASCII longitudes are integer-truncated. Transposed and reversed to north-up; seam columns averaged with differences recorded. Generated PNG pixels by numerical bilinear resampling at pixel centres, avoiding a half-cell registration shift.
limitations: Model means omit extremes; no live weather, route-scale accuracy or climate routing penalty. High-resolution topographic correction is not high-resolution meteorology.
usage: MCD © LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES. Noncommercial scientific use with attribution and notification. User confirmed author notification sent on 2026-11-14. Terms: https://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mars/access ; credits: https://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/credit.html

title: Geologic map of Mars · SIM 3292
institution: Tanaka et al. (2014) · U.S. Geological Survey
description: The USGS global geologic map identifies 44 surface units and their mapped relationships. The atlas uses the USGS polygon collection and its published unit colours.
format: GeoJSON source polygons; indexed numeric grid and matching PNG
units: USGS unit codes, descriptions and polygon IDs
crs: Mars IAU:49900 planetocentric coordinates, east positive
processing: Assign the source polygon at each derivative cell centre. Retain original feature IDs and codes.
limitations: Map units and boundaries are regional interpretations. Effective map accuracy varies and has not been independently established.
usage: Public domain. Credit Tanaka et al. (2014) and USGS. https://www.usgs.gov/media/images/usgs-sim-3292-geologic-map-mars

title: Terra Sirenum CRISM mineral observations
description: The catalogue gives the centres of targeted CRISM images analysed in the Terra Sirenum study and the authors’ mineral interpretations. Approximate or possible detections retain their qualifiers.
format: Published CSV and a static point catalogue
resolution: Published coordinate precision; point accuracy unknown
processing: Retain mineral records and their original interpretation and CRISM image IDs. Exclude blank, ice-only and no-detection entries.
limitations: Markers locate image centres. The footprint of a spectral detection, sampling coordinates and observations outside the study remain unavailable.
usage: CC0 1.0 CaltechDATA deposit. Credit Leask et al. and the MRO CRISM team.

title: Chloride-bearing deposit catalogue
institution: Leask & Ehlmann (2021), after Osterloo et al. (2010) · CaltechDATA

format: Published CSV and a static point catalogue
coverage: Chloride sites previously mapped in THEMIS imagery
resolution: Source catalogue coordinates; point accuracy and footprints unavailable
processing: Retain latitude, longitude, source feature ID and label from the numerical catalogue.
limitations: A catalogue marker denotes a geological interpretation and leaves the occurrence extent and access unassessed.
usage: CC0 1.0 CaltechDATA deposit. Credit Leask & Ehlmann, Osterloo et al. and the THEMIS team.

title: Hydrated mineral sites from OMEGA and CRISM
institution: Carter et al. (2013) · ESA Mars Express · NASA MRO · NASA PDS
description: PDS HYDROUS_SITES_GEO_MAP release and revision 0001 gives coordinates of hydrated mineral detections from OMEGA and CRISM. Instrument product IDs are preserved per site.
format: PDS CSV and label, packaged as a static point catalogue
coverage: Targeted detections across Mars, with uneven survey coverage
resolution: 0.01° printed coordinate precision. Absolute accuracy is unknown.
crs: Planetocentric latitude and signed east longitude
processing: 1,855 source rows yield 1,851 distinct records after four exact repeats are merged. All source row numbers are retained.
limitations: The table supplies no mineral species, detection boundaries or ground sampling targets. Route distance to a record is research context with zero ranking weight.
usage: NASA Open Data lists this archive as US public domain. Credit Carter et al. and the ESA OMEGA and NASA CRISM teams.

title: Mars nightside apparent thermal inertia
institution: Putzig, Mellon, Heet and Ward (2009) · NASA PDS
description: GLOBAL_TI_NIGHT_2007 modelled from TES thermal bolometer observations in 1999–2004. The matching interpolation mask identifies source pixels with direct observation support.
format: PDS3 labels, signed 16-bit image and 8-bit binary mask; compressed numerical grid and matching PNG
coverage: Global source footprint. The atlas shows 53.0% of Mars by area after requiring full direct support per derivative cell.
crs: Planetocentric Mars, simple cylindrical, east positive
processing: Area-weight each 5 × 5 source block, require all source pixels to pass the mask, round to whole thermal inertia units and leave gaps transparent.
limitations: Apparent thermal response varies with surface heterogeneity. Local bearing strength, traction and traversal conditions remain unassessed.
usage: Public NASA PDS mission product MGS-M-TES-5-TIMAP-V1.0. Retain the creators’ citation and archive credit.

title: TES dust-cover index
description: The authors’ spectral index averages TES emissivity over 1,350–1,400 cm⁻¹. The 16-pixel/degree source excludes spectra above stated atmospheric dust and ice-cloud opacity limits.
format: PDS and VICAR source arrays and original browse maps
coverage: Global source layout, valid-data mask unresolved
crs: ASU catalogue lists planetocentric simple cylindrical, −180° to 180° E
processing: The downloaded PDS and VICAR arrays agree. The atlas links to the original product.
limitations: The numerical label gives no missing-data code. A repeated lower value covers uniform polar rows. The Mars Trek metadata lists private access and use terms as TBD. Redistribution terms for the ASU download remain unverified.
usage: Follow ASU guidance and credit Ruff & Christensen. Source-only reference.

title: Photogeologic Map of the Perseverance Rover Field Site in Jezero Crater
institution: Stack et al. (2020), Space Science Reviews; Mars 2020 science team
description: Table 2 representative type locations for D-tnl, D-tkl and D-tcl delta units support local Ancient Water and Sedimentary Geology objectives. Interpretations are geological evidence, not biosignature probabilities. DOI 10.1007/s11214-020-00739-x.
format: Published numerical type locations and paraphrased unit interpretations
resolution: Map scale 1:5000; type coordinates rounded to 0.001°, not positional accuracy
units: East longitude, north planetocentric latitude in degrees
crs: Mars planetocentric / east-positive coordinates; paper map extent used to resolve mislabeled lat/lon column order
processing: Selected three published type outcrops; no figure colours or crater-centre coordinates converted to sample sites
limitations: Representative type positions, not exact sampling sites, established access points or safe locations. Alignment accuracy not independently measured.
usage: Factual locations and paraphrased interpretations with citation; original publication terms apply. No paper figures redistributed.
